items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: playing “Temptation” for a stripper was just remembering what I heard Earl Bostic, how he played it, that’s how I played it.

ctx.x: You know he can do that really easy. So but that’s when I learned it, I would say that was in high school. I was playing strip shows at that time, I was doing it six nights a week as a sophomore in high school, doing the strip shows at McMann’s, and my teacher, the guy that had a heart attack, that Joey Camara, had a heart attack and they needed somebody right away and my teacher got the call from Hill Munter who was this piano player who I learned a lot from, oh what a great guy he was too. Terrific cat. And he…

tunes, you’re knowing tunes that you have to insert on an automatic level, and you’re interpreting this chart that you can barely even see. And Hill just would teach me relax, he says, this is what you do, you go through this number, and I got it down. I mean I was very good at it and I knew all the tunes, you know, playing “Temptation” for a stripper was just remembering what I heard Earl Bostic, how he played it, that’s how I played it. I put the growl in there and just played it like, and people used to flip.
I bet you learned to project in that situation.
